findings.view: C:\dev\fable-space-game\out\screens\ocean\perf-splash-1440p.png (foreground patches around native px 830,1010 and the streak at 2430,915); overcast.png (410,652); night.png (125,552 / 110,655 / 1030,497); stability-animated.png (160,503 / 365,640); splash.png (1117,457 / 430,610); refraction.png (80,427)
findings.defect: Every whitecap and foam patch near the camera is a smooth, soft-edged white smudge with no internal structure: cotton-wool blobs in the splashdown close-up, a perfect blurred oval under overcast, smeared streaks at night and with TAA running. No bubbles, no lace, no holes, no streaking, no thickness variation. It reads as an out-of-focus sprite painted on the water, at the exact place the mission ends.
findings.realReference: Recovery-ship and swimmer footage of Apollo, Orion and Dragon splashdowns, and any deck-level photograph: fresh foam is opaque white with crisp ragged edges on the breaking crest; within a second or two it opens into a sharp cellular net of bubble rafts with dark water showing through, pulled into streaks down-wind; aged foam is a thin grey-green lace. Under moonlight foam is a faint grey, far below the glitter.
findings.likelyCause: Foam coverage exists only at the FFT cascade texel size: cascade 1 is 8192/29 m over 256 px = 1.1 m per texel, cascade 0 is 4.6 m, cascade 2 is 0.28 m (src/render/ocean/shaders/fftWgsl.ts lines 184-189, src/render/ocean/fft.ts), bilinearly magnified. The 'lace' in src/render/ocean/shaders/surfaceWgsl.ts fs() (laceN from der.z + der.w with OCEAN_LACE_WEIGHT, then smoothstep(th - hw, th + hw, laceN) with hw = 0.08 + 0.6 sqrt(laceLost)) is itself a smooth band-limited field and is widened wherever it is filtered, so the threshold never makes a hard cell edge. Foam is shaded as a flat Lambert term (waterBrdf.ts brdfWaterDirect: foamAlbedo / PI * max(dot(up, l), 0)) with no detail normal and no thickness. TAA smears what is left (stability-animated.png).
findings.fixDirection: Add a real foam detail layer in the forward pass: two or three octaves of tiling cellular bubble lace (procedural Worley or a baked tile, periods about 2 m, 0.5 m and 0.12 m) advected in Lagrangian plane coordinates, and use coverage as the THRESHOLD of that detail (foam = smoothstep(1 - c, 1 - c + one pixel footprint, detail)), so thick foam is solid and thin foam is lace with hard edges. Keep two states: the active breaker (thick, bright, crest-aligned) and residual foam that decays over 5-10 s through lace to nothing while drifting down-wind. Shade foam with its own bumpy normal and a thickness-dependent albedo (about 0.9 fresh, 0.3 lace), and give foam pixels the full TAA reactive value. Keep the statistical term only where a pixel cannot resolve 0.5 m.

findings.defect: Between 100 m and 3 km (the whole parachute descent) the sun path is a continuous matte grey sheet crossed by dark squiggly 'worm' lines; straight down from 150 m it reads as embossed stucco, from 3 km as a bump-mapped plastic sheet. Nothing reaches white: the brightest 0.5 % of the frame is sRGB 132 (alt500), 128 (alt3k), 153 (climb-273m). There is no glitter at all, and the contrast is inverted against reality: a bright continuous ground with dark lines instead of dark water carrying brilliant points.
findings.realReference: Helicopter, aircraft and parachute-camera footage from 100 m to 3 km: the sun path is thousands of discrete saturated sparkles on dark blue water, densest at the mirror point and thinning outward, each one clipped with glare, twinkling frame to frame; between them the water stays dark. From 3 km it is a grainy, scintillating silver. It becomes a smooth sheen only from tens of kilometres.
findings.likelyCause: src/render/ocean/shaders/waterBrdf.ts puts every slope the normal does not resolve into one smooth GGX lobe (waterAlpha: alpha^2 = KAPPA^2 x Cox-Munk x field x (1 - s.roughness)). At 0.2-5 m pixel footprints the capillary and short-gravity variance (about half of Cox-Munk: capillary layers 0.0152 plus unresolvedSlopeVariance 0.0025) is drawn as its per-pixel MEAN, so radiance never exceeds a few times the mean. Physically a 1 m^2 footprint holds a few hundred 5 cm facets and the chance that one of them mirrors the 0.53 deg sun is about 1e-4 at the peak: roughly 3 % of pixels should carry a sparkle about 30x the mean at 500 m, about one per pixel at 3 km. The lab presets also lock EV 15 (labs/ocean/main.ts PRESETS alt500..leo), which parks the mean glint at mid-grey.
findings.fixDirection: Add a stochastic glint term to brdfWaterDirect for the unresolved variance: per planet-fixed cell of about the footprint size, draw a Poisson count of facets that fall inside the sun's solid angle (mean = N_facets x D(h) x Omega_sun / 4, N from footprint area over a facet area of about (5 cm)^2), re-hashed about 15 times a second for twinkle, radiance = count x sun radiance x Fresnel x the facet's share; keep the smooth lobe only as the expectation where the mean count is above about 5, so energy is unchanged. Clamp through writeHdr and let bloom do the glare. The same function still yields the broad orbital glint (mean count is huge there). Then re-shoot 150 m, 500 m and 3 km at the exposure the game's meter chooses, not EV 15.

findings.defect: From 5 to 30 km the sea is a blue-grey gradient with a fog-like grey smudge where the glint should be (brightest 0.5 % of the frame: sRGB 105 at 10 km, 106 at 30 km). At 10 km the lower 40 % of the frame has a fine embossed wave texture with a compact bright spot (560,500 in alt10k.png), and above an arc at 10.5-15 km range it turns into smooth cloud-like blobs: two different materials meeting along an arc, obvious when contrast-stretched and visible without. At 30 km one blob is a squarish noise cell (685,550). PROMPT.txt forbids blue gradients; the hand-off lists the texture change as a known weakness, but a player sees it in mid-screen during descent and ascent over water.
findings.realReference: Airliner-window, high-altitude-balloon and booster-camera footage from 10-30 km: the glint is a bright silver-white patch that carries crisp fine structure everywhere: parallel swell lines, wind rows, sharp-edged slicks and current fronts, ship wakes, cloud shadows; outside it the sea is deep blue with visible swell texture and whitecap speckle. The character does not change with range, it only compresses.
findings.likelyCause: The contract-driven detail fade (src/render/ocean/shaders/waves.ts oceanDetail: 1 inside 0.7 x fadeStart, 0 at fadeStart = 15 km; data detailFadeFraction 0.7) removes every resolved normal (swell, long-wave layer, cascade 0) by DISTANCE, not by pixel footprint. Beyond it the far sheet is shaded with a flat normal and only the roughness field of waterBrdf.ts (WATER_FIELD_WGSL): smooth gradient-noise octaves that change the lobe WIDTH by at most about 40 % (windVariability 0.35, gustVariability 0.3, slickStrength 0.35). Width modulation of a broad lobe gives low-contrast blurry blobs; nothing tilts the mean normal, so there are no wave lines, although the 52-180 m swell and the long-wave slopes are resolvable at 10-40 m pixels. The lab sky haze (labs/ocean/labSky.ts) lowers contrast further; budget-leo.png and budget-reentry-end.png in out/screens/integration show the far sea is acceptable once clouds and land carry the frame, so the fault is the open-water 5-30 km range.
findings.fixDirection: Put resolved long-wave structure into brdf_water itself so the deferred far sheet has it: evaluate the swell gradient analytically and sample the long-wave slopes layer in planet-fixed coordinates in the deferred path, both band-limited by the pixel footprint, and drive the forward detail fade by footprint as well, so near and far use the same normals at fadeStart (the 2 % hand-over criterion then holds by construction). Add anisotropic, hard-edged content to the field: wind rows along the wind at 100-300 m spacing, slick boundaries from thresholded domain-warped noise instead of smoothstep blobs, and a much stronger calm contrast (slick variance x 0.2-0.3). Re-judge 3, 10 and 30 km in the integrated app with the real atmosphere and clouds.

findings.defect: Whitecaps are a star field: hundreds of isolated 1-2 px white pinpoints plus a few round 'popcorn' blobs, uniformly sprinkled, with no shape, no direction and no trails. The debug view of the foam mask literally looks like a night sky with two globular clusters. The mean coverage is calibrated (0.117 %), the size and shape distribution is not.
findings.realReference: At 7 m/s (Beaufort 4, 'fairly frequent white horses') whitecaps seen from 100-500 m are crest-aligned crescents and bars 2-10 m long, perpendicular to the wind, each leaving a fading foam patch and a streak down-wind; a frame holds tens of distinct elongated strokes at different ages, not hundreds of dots.
findings.likelyCause: Foam is bred per cascade where that cascade's own Jacobian falls foamSigma = 3.0 standard deviations below 1 (fftWgsl.ts line 187; data/defs/render/earth.ocean.json foamSigma 3.0, foamRampSigma 0.8): only isolated extreme-tail texels fire. Breaking is not tied to the dominant waves (the swell and the long-wave layer never contribute), nothing spreads foam along the crest or advects it, and it decays at 0.6 /s in place.
findings.fixDirection: Compute breaking from the combined field: sum of the cascades' convergence plus the local steepness and crest proximity of the swell and long-wave layer, thresholded lower (about 1.5-2 sigma) after a low-pass along the crest direction so that whole crest segments fire; keep a second, longer-lived residual layer (5-10 s) that drifts down-wind. Re-calibrate the mean to Monahan afterwards and add a spec on the patch-size distribution (for example median connected foam area above 3 m^2 from 150 m).

findings.defect: The shallowest water is drawn as terraces: three or four flat-coloured bands (tan, brown, olive, green) with crisp edges that follow depth contours like a topographic map, some edges with a pixel sawtooth. Further out, standing in the shallows, large tan and teal patches meet along crisp lines. Note: perf-coast-1440p.png is from the perf project (22:09, two minutes before the last shader edit, which only changed the refraction trust near the frame border); confirm on a fresh shot from 60 m.
findings.realReference: Aerial and drone photographs of a sandy shelf: a continuous gradient from wet-sand tan through pale yellow-green and aqua to turquoise and blue, with no steps; the only lines are the swash edge and real bottom features (ripples, weed, rock).
findings.likelyCause: src/render/ocean/shaders/surfaceWgsl.ts line 424: s.param = round(encodeWaterDepth(max(seaDepth, 0.0)) * 255.0) / 255.0. The near field quantises its float seabed depth to the G-buffer's 8-bit sqrt encoding (WATER_DEPTH_ENCODE_MAX 200 m: steps of 5-25 cm between 0.1 and 5 m), and the red channel changes by 10-20 % per step at the data's 0.45 /m absorption. The remaining patches are the difference between the modelled bottom and the screen-space refracted bed that the hand-off already admits (blended by 'conf').
findings.fixDirection: Use the continuous depth inside fadeStart: blend the quantised value in only as detail goes to 0 (mix(quantised, exact, detail)), or pass the depth to the forward variant of the chunk as a private float instead of s.param; the 8-bit semantics are only needed where the forward surface must equal the deferred sheet. Then make the two bottom models agree in colour (same albedo, same attenuation path) so the confidence blend has nothing to show.

findings.view: C:\dev\fable-space-game\out\screens\ocean\refraction.png (dark ellipse at 640,315; yellow-green ghost at 640,250); handover-refraction.png (dark blob at 622,285; ghost at 640,271)
findings.defect: A submerged yellow ball in turquoise water shows as a hard-edged DARK BLUE silhouette at its unrefracted screen position (a hole in the sea, pixel-exact outline of the G-buffer object), with the actual refracted image as a separate smear above it. Anything non-terrain under shallow water (pad and pier structures, a hull in the shallows, floats, sunk parachutes) will punch the same dark stencil.
findings.realReference: Through 1-2 m of clear water a yellow or white object looks green-yellow or pale aqua, displaced and vertically squeezed toward the horizon, wobbling with the waves, and the water in front of it keeps the colour of the bottom seen past it. There is never a dark cut-out.
findings.likelyCause: surfaceWgsl.ts fs(): for a G-buffer pixel that is not terrain, 'seabed' is false, so seaDepth stays OCEAN_DEEP (10 km) and s.param encodes optically deep water with s.albedo = 0: the body colour of those pixels is the deep-ocean scatter (dark blue) while the neighbours get the bright shallow-sand model. The refraction term (lit += (seen * att - bottomFar) * conf) only replaces the BOTTOM part (bottomFar is 0 here), never the column term, so the deep-water scatter stays under whatever the march found.
findings.fixDirection: When the pixel under the water is an object, take the water column from the refraction march: use hitDepth (tHit * cosT) for the body/column term of that pixel (so in-scatter is that of a 1-2 m column), and when the refracted ray passes the object and reaches the seabed use the seabed's depth and albedo from the hit pixel's G-buffer. Add a spec: mean colour inside the ball's unrefracted silhouette within a few percent of the surrounding water.

findings.view: C:\dev\fable-space-game\out\screens\ocean\overcast.png (y 285-380); shore.png (y 300-420); refraction.png (y 215-420); perf-coast-1440p.png (far sea, native y 560-720); sunset.png (y 335-360)
findings.defect: At grazing angles the water is shaded the wrong way round. Thin dark slate 'hairlines' (sRGB 39,50,64 against a median 26,121,115 in refraction.png; 73,75,77 against 108,110,115 in overcast.png) run across the middle distance like scratches, and the sea gets darker and greyer toward the horizon: 78,86,91 against a sky of 156,157,151 just above it at 60 m (perf-coast), 50,35,8 against 147,107,25 at sunset.
findings.realReference: At low angles water is a mirror: wave backs and distant water reflect the bright sky just above the horizon and are the LIGHTEST parts of the scene, wave fronts facing the viewer are the dark, see-through parts and form broad soft bands, and the sea brightens and loses saturation toward the horizon (effective reflectance of a 7 m/s sea near the horizon is about 0.25-0.35 of a sky that is brighter low down).
findings.likelyCause: Hypothesis from the code (verify with setDebugView('skyReflection')): (1) waterBrdf.ts brdfWaterAmbient uses the generic split-sum fit envBrdfApprox(sqrt(alpha), NoV) with F0 0.02, which caps the reflectance at about 0.45 for the near field (rough 0.25) and 0.14 for the far sheet (rough 0.5) however grazing the view, where flat-water Fresnel is 0.6-0.9; (2) with an environment probe published, waterSkyRadiance samples envProbeCube at mip sqrt(alpha) x (levels - 1), whose trilinear footprint near the horizon averages in the dark lower hemisphere, then x 0.85 for folded rays; (3) shading normals that face away from the viewer (most of them at 1-5 deg grazing) keep NoV clamped at 1e-4, so the body term's transmission goes to zero and only that dim reflection is left: the dark lines.
findings.fixDirection: For water replace the split-sum factor by a rough-sea Fresnel: mean Fresnel over the visible facets (a small 2-D fit in NoV and slope sigma, or Schlick evaluated at max(NoV, about 1.2 sigma)); bend shading normals into the visible hemisphere before reflect/refract; sample the reflected sky with a horizon-clamped lobe (sky-view table, or a probe lookup that never blends the below-horizon half) and raise the mean reflected direction by the visible-normal shift at grazing angles. Check against a photograph: sea next to the horizon at about a third of the adjacent sky's luminance in clear midday, brighter than the nearer water.

findings.view: C:\dev\fable-space-game\out\screens\ocean\perf-splash-1440p.png (native px 1300-2560, 540-850); also midday.png (y 262-330) and splash.png (y 265-330) at 720p
findings.defect: The middle distance (about 20-100 m from a 3 m camera) is covered in regular 1-2 px horizontal stripes alternating khaki-grey and blue, like interlacing or woven cloth. In a still it reads as a texture artefact; in motion it will crawl. Nearer the camera the capillary detail has a regular dashed 'denim' weave.
findings.realReference: A real lens averages the compressed far waves into soft, irregular light and dark bands several pixels deep; there is no row-locked pattern, and the near surface shows smooth glassy facets with irregular patches of ripples, not an even weave.
findings.likelyCause: surfaceWgsl.ts fs(): each layer's lod is log2(max(fpMin, fpMaj / 4) x 256 / L) with a 4x anisotropic sampler, so slopes are kept up to the pixel Nyquist along the foreshortened axis (about 64 % of a 2 px wave survives the 4-tap box); oceanSwellEval's band limit exp(-0.125 (k x fpMaj)^2) (waves.ts) is equally generous. At grazing angles Fresnel x sky colour is a steep nonlinear function of the along-view slope, so each row point-samples a different wave phase. The weave near the camera is the two capillary copies of the finest cascade, which tile every 18.2 m / 4.2 = 4.3 m and 18.2 m / 17.6 = 1.04 m (oceanFeature.ts lines 436-437, capillaryScale 4.2).
findings.fixDirection: Band-limit along the major axis at 4 px per wavelength or more (lod bias +1 once the footprint anisotropy exceeds 4, or 16x anisotropy; swell filter width about 2 x fpMaj), return the removed variance to the lobe as the bookkeeping already does, and shade the mean (LEAN-style: widen the reflection lookup and Fresnel by the along-view slope variance of the footprint) rather than a point sample. Break the capillary tiling: modulate its amplitude by the short gravity waves (ripples ride the forward faces, troughs are glassy) and use non-repeating blends of more than two rotations.

findings.view: C:\dev\fable-space-game\out\screens\ocean\splash.png (capsule at 390-490, 295-375); perf-splash-1440p.png (capsule at native 780-980, 520-670); markers-swell-only.png and markers-with-chop.png (orange spheres)
findings.defect: The floating capsule looks pasted onto the sea. The water shows no reflection of the white hull or of the orange spheres (not even on the mirror-flat surface of markers-swell-only.png), no darkening of the water beside the hull, a waterline that is a clean geometric ellipse, and a foam ring made of flat pure-white scraps with hard edges. No aqua glow of the submerged hull through the water and no visible wet band on the hull.
findings.realReference: Recovery footage: the capsule's white and orange reflect in the water in front of it as a broken, shimmering streak; the water against the hull is darker (it reflects the hull's shadowed side instead of the sky) and laps up and down leaving a glossy wet band; the submerged heat shield shows as a pale aqua halo from above; foam and dye spread as lacy sheets, not confetti.
findings.likelyCause: The forward pass has no reflection of scene objects: waterSkyRadiance (waterBrdf.ts) reads only the sky table or probe. Wake and ripple foam go through the same smooth coverage as finding 1 (wake = smoothstep(1 - w, 1 - w + 0.35, laceN) in surfaceWgsl.ts). The hull is the lab's untextured prop, so the wet line cannot be judged here.
findings.fixDirection: Add a short screen-space reflection march against 'scene.colorCopy' and 'scene.depthOpaque' in the forward pass for the near field (a dozen steps, only for reflected rays within about 30 deg of the horizon and within a few hull radii of a vessel slot from 'ocean.wetness'), falling back to the sky; where the march misses, occlude the sky by the vessel's bounding shape so water next to the hull darkens. Give wake foam the detail treatment of finding 1. Re-shoot the splash preset with the real capsule and chutes from the vehicle package.

findings.view: C:\dev\fable-space-game\out\screens\ocean\shore.png (waterline along y 300, no foam at all); shoreAlong.png (white fringe 0-720, 330-410); perf-coast-1440p.png; corroborated by C:\dev\fable-space-game\out\screens\integration\water-shoreline-200m.png (a uniform white outline traced along the whole coast)
findings.defect: The shore has no surf. The sea meets the sand along a razor edge; where foam exists it is a thin white fringe hugging the waterline like an outline stroke, absent on other stretches. No breaking waves, no run-up sheets, no wet sand.
findings.realReference: Even on a calm day swell shoals, steepens and breaks in one or more lines parallel to the beach; white bores run up as thin sheets with lacy leading edges, drain back and leave dark, glossy wet sand; from 200 m the surf zone is a streaky white band tens of metres wide.
findings.likelyCause: surfaceWgsl.ts lines 376-382: shore foam is swash = 1 - smoothstep(0, shoreFoamDepthM (0.8 m), dynDepth), a function of local depth only, so it is a constant-depth contour: an outline. TMA attenuation removes the chop in the shallows and the four swell sinusoids never shoal, steepen or break. Nothing is published for the terrain to wet the sand.
findings.fixDirection: Drive a surf zone from the swell phase: where depth falls below about 1.3 x the local swell height, spawn breaker lines that travel shoreward at sqrt(g h) as foam bores (position from the swell phase, width growing toward shore), a run-up sheet whose reach oscillates with that phase and leaves residual lace, and publish a shore wetness band (highest recent run-up) for the terrain to darken and gloss the sand. From altitude, scale the white band with the shelf slope instead of a fixed 0.8 m depth.

findings.view: C:\dev\fable-space-game\out\screens\ocean\climb-273m.png (parallel stripes at 600-950, 300-520); alt500.png; alt3k.png (regular pillow lattice); midday.png, splash.png, stability-animated.png (ruler-straight horizon, nothing ever occluded)
findings.defect: The sea has no real waves. From 2 m it is a nearly flat sheet with fine noise on top: the horizon is a ruled line and no crest ever hides the base of the capsule or the water behind it. From 270 m to 3 km the long waves show as evenly spaced parallel stripes and a regular lattice. The hand-off lists this as scheduled (request ocean-5 with the lead); it is still what a player sees.
findings.realReference: A 7 m/s wind sea has a significant height of 1-1.6 m with short-crested, irregular waves in groups: from 2 m eye height nearby crests rise toward eye level, hide the troughs behind them and parts of a floating capsule, and make the horizon slightly ragged; from the air crests are broken segments of varying length and no two stay parallel for long.
findings.likelyCause: data/defs/bodies/earth.json ocean.swell is four sinusoids (180/95/52/28 m, amplitudes 0.45/0.30/0.22/0.15 m, steepness ak at most 0.034) and carries all height above 25 m; the FFT heights are 0.11 m rms; the long-wave layer added after the review is normals only (no parallax, no occlusion, no silhouette).
findings.fixDirection: Lead: adopt at least 8 swell components (MAX_SWELL) with non-commensurate wavelengths around the spectrum's 70 m peak, directional spread of about +-30 deg and realistic steepness, or let physics sample a shared low-resolution spectral height field for 25-200 m. Within the ocean's paths, if the lead agrees: draw the long-wave layer's HEIGHT too, blended to pure swell within about 10 hull radii of any vessel so the 5 cm waterline criterion still holds where it matters, and report it with the FFT term.

findings.defect: Shallow water over sand is one flat, saturated teal with a soft blurred mottle, like tinted paint: no caustics, no readable bottom, no depth gradation across 0-3 m, and no sparkle on top to give the surface a plane. In shoreAlong.png the lower right is streaky as if motion-blurred.
findings.realReference: Sunlit water 0.5-5 m deep over pale sand shows a bright, sharp, moving caustic net on the bottom, the bottom's own ripples and dark patches bent by the waves, crisp sky reflections and sun points on the surface, and a strong gradation from near-colourless at the edge through aqua to blue-green.
findings.likelyCause: The refracted bed radiance (seen * att in surfaceWgsl.ts) and the modelled bottom term have no focusing term: the seabed is lit by the deferred pass as if dry. Refraction samples are bilinear lookups stretched by the distortion, and the glint lobe on top is the smooth mean of finding 2.
findings.fixDirection: Multiply the refracted and modelled bottom radiance by a caustic factor from the wave field: 1 / |det(I + d x Hessian(h))| clamped, with d = depth / cos(refracted sun angle), from the derivatives of cascades 2-3 projected along the refracted sun direction, fading out by about 8 m depth and with cloud shadow. Sharpen the refraction lookup (one extra refinement step, no chromatic spread beyond a pixel) and rely on the glint term for surface sparkle.

findings.defect: From orbit the glint is a dim grey disc (brightest 0.5 % of the frame sRGB 90 at LEO) holding a few soft amoeba-shaped blobs; outside it the slicks are faint soft specks that only show when the contrast is stretched. At 100 km it is a smooth beige column (the stepped vertical edges at x 490/740/850 are probably the lab sky's table; check in the integrated app). It is the recognisable look of thresholded Perlin noise, not of sea surface.
findings.realReference: ISS, Gemini and Apollo sunglint photographs: a silver-white, often saturated core with crisp texture: long curved slick lines, packets of internal waves (parallel arcs 0.5-2 km apart), ship and island wakes many kilometres long, calm tongues in the lee of land, eddies traced by slicks, cloud shadows. Slicks are mirror-bright inside the glint and near-black just outside it.
findings.likelyCause: WATER_FIELD_WGSL in waterBrdf.ts: isotropic low-order gradient noise passed through smoothsteps, with small amplitudes (wind exp(0.35 n), slick 1 - 0.35 s), no line features, no flow-like warping, no dependence on coast or islands; from orbit only four octaves remain.
findings.fixDirection: Warp the slick coordinates with a curl-noise flow so they form eddies and fronts, use ridged noise for hard-edged filament lines, add internal-wave packets as sets of parallel arcs in a few places, raise the calm contrast (variance x 0.2-0.3 in slicks), and add lee calm zones from the terrain's land mask if the core can supply one. Compare side by side with two or three ISS glint frames at the meter's exposure.

findings.view: C:\dev\fable-space-game\out\screens\ocean\alt500.png .. leo.png (exposure); refr-diag-on.png, refr-diag-off.png, refr-diag-flat-on.png (stale); glint-leo.png and handover-near-off.png (overlay); perf-splash-1440p.png, perf-coast-1440p.png, perf-10km-1440p.png (not regenerated)
findings.defect: Review hygiene that hides or misstates the look. (a) The altitude presets lock EV 15, about 1.5-2 stops darker than a camera metering those scenes, so every altitude shot is a dull grey-blue and cannot be judged against photographs. (b) Three refr-diag-*.png files from 10 Nov 19:15 belong to a deleted diag spec and show old faults (tiled seams, a green ball); no current spec writes them. (c) The lab overlay prints 'camera NaN m above the sea' whenever the near field is off. (d) The three perf-*-1440p.png shots are the only 1440p images and are written only by the perf project, so they predate the last shader edit. For the record: the functional specs were re-run through the gate for this review, 27 passed, and all 29 functional screenshots are current; six integration screenshots were also looked at for context.
findings.realReference: A reviewed screenshot set should show what the player's camera would show: metered exposure, current code, no debug text over the judged shots, and one native-resolution image per reviewed scene.
findings.likelyCause: labs/ocean/main.ts PRESETS (ev: 15 on alt500..leo); out/screens/ocean is never cleaned; oceanFeature.ts line 358 reports cameraHeight NaN when no near-field state exists; tests/browser/ocean/screens.spec.ts shoots at 1280 x 720 only.
findings.fixDirection: Let the altitude presets use the renderer's meter (or EV 12.5-13 with the reason stated), delete the stale refr-diag files, print the real camera height in the overlay, and add 1440p variants of splash, shore and alt10k to screens.spec.ts so close-up foam, shoreline and hand-over are always judged at native resolution.
